creator: robert.triebwasser
title: Argues email-based AI agents beat voice assistants (ChatGPT Dots) for business: cc an agent into any email thread (which already holds people, files, context) and ask it to finish a deck or chase colleagues; demo shows 'Riley (AI Assistant)' cc'd in Outlook

tools.name: ChatGPT Dots
tools.detail: Voice assistant; creator spent 30 min on a call with it at the airport; 'good personal assistant, not a business assistant'

tools.name: Email agent 'Riley (AI Assistant)'
tools.detail: Mock Outlook reply: To Mark Davies, Sarah Mitchell; Cc 'Riley (AI Assistant)'; body 'Riley, can you finish the lau[nch deck]...'; tool behind it not named (creator sells a tutorial)

tools.name: Outlook / Gmail
tools.detail: Mock inboxes used for the demo

claims: Email-based agents are '10 times more powerful' than voice models for business
The average working professional gets 121 emails a day
Every email thread is a mini project: relevant people, files, attachments and long-running context already present
Cc an agent into the thread and ask it to pick up tasks (finish a PowerPoint, follow up with staff when work is incomplete); it works in the background like a coworker
how_to_steps: Give the agent its own mailbox/address
Cc it on a thread and address it by name with a task ('Riley, can you finish the launch deck')
Agent reads thread + attachments, does the work, and follows up with colleagues on incomplete items
on_screen_only: 'Voice agent ON A CALL 29:53' waveform widget over an airport shot; 'ChatGPT Dots' pill

Outlook inbox mock: Sarah Mitchell 'Q4 budget review', James Carter 'RE: Client proposal', Priya Shah 'Invoice #2043', Mark Davies 'RE: Launch timeline', Olivia Brooks, Daniel Kim 'Contract for review', Team Calendar, Emma Rodriguez, Alex Turner, Nina Patel, Chris Walker, HR Team
Stat card: 'THE AVERAGE WORKING PROFESSIONAL 121 emails a day - Sent and received, every working day'
Gmail thread 'Q4 launch plan' (Project label, 6 people, attachments Launch-Deck.pptx, Budget.xlsx, Contract.pdf, Product-shots.zip)
Outlook compose: To Mark Davies, Sarah Mitchell; Cc Riley (AI Assistant); 'RE: Q4 launch plan - Riley, can you finish the lau...'
Bottom-right comment prompt: 'COMMENT EMAIL step-by-step tutorial'
cta: Comment 'email' for a tutorial; join community; follow

relevance.why: Email-native agent is a practical pattern for a solo founder handling client/vendor threads; Haji liked a Town chief-of-staff app and Gmail-MCP Jarvis, so the idea is familiar, but the 'cc the agent into a thread' interaction is a clean UX for delegating.

implement_score.why: Doable with existing pieces: a dedicated mailbox + Gmail MCP/Zapier trigger that wakes a Claude Code routine when the agent address is cc'd, reads the thread and attachments, drafts output for approval. Half a day; keep send rights gated (see spend/send warnings).

verify: What platform the creator's 'Riley' runs on (Hermes with email channel?) and whether the tutorial is paid
Source of the '121 emails a day' statistic
Security: a cc'd agent reading all thread content is a prompt-injection surface; needs allowlists

gap.what: Liked set has email-reading assistants and Jarvis-with-Gmail, but not the 'cc the agent into existing threads' delegation pattern as the primary interface, nor the voice-vs-email argument for business use.
